prerequisites: Basic knowledge of metallic material properties, reading and interpretation of technical documentation, and graphic representation
An active attitude towards laboratory work, rigorous compliance with safety standards, technical observation of processes and defects, and interpretation of inspection results
Ability to work in a team and apply knowledge of materials, physics, and manufacturing to solve problems related to welded joints
Sensitivity towards quality, safety, sustainability, and environmental impact aspects associated with welding processes and industrial manufacturing

learning_outcomes.text: Scientific and technological knowledge about welding processes. Welding metallurgy. Weldability of different materials and application of the most common inspection procedures for evaluating the quality of welded joints and ensuring quality requirements.
Ability to write and develop procedures for the welding manufacturing of structures, pressure vessels, and other industrial equipment.
Define processes and establish welding procedures, determining phases, operations, equipment, and tools, considering quality and economic criteria.
Ability to handle specifications and standards related to the construction and quality of welded joints.

syllabus_topics: Manual arc welding with coated electrode.
Submerged arc, electroslag, and electrogas welding processes.
High energy density welding processes: electron beam, laser, and plasma.
Thermal spray and cold spray overlays.

assessment_methods.method: Written test Block I: welding processes I and weldability (EP1)
Written test Block II: defectology and inspection of welded joints (EP2)
Evaluation of Block III: welding processes II, special processes and related techniques (EP3)

assessment_rules: All evaluable activities are graded on a scale of 10 points. For the ordinary call with a final written test, the final grade (C) is calculated as: C = 0.15·EP1 + 0.10·EP2 + 0.15·EP3 + 0.10·L + 0.50·PG. To pass, C must be 5 or higher, the final written test (PG) must be 4.5 or higher, and the laboratory evaluation (L) must be 5 or higher. For the extraordinary call, the final grade is C = 0.90·PE + 0.10·LExtra, requiring C >= 5 and LExtra >= 5. Laboratory grades (L) can be carried over, but EP1, EP2, EP3, and PG grades are only valid for the current academic year. Attendance to laboratory sessions is mandatory.
